records.verificationNote: Generic quetiapine IR is covered without PA up to 3 units/day (MHDL 'PA - 3 units/day'; table reference quantity limit). Quantity-limit PA is read as applying above the limit (MHDL SmartPA note: claims within limits usually process without PA). Quetiapine checked against the drug list (drugId 1618: PA 3 units/day), consistent. Brand Vraylar, Rexulti, Caplyta and Lybalvi carry PD (preferred drug) but still require PA. Criteria paragraphs for individual drugs were not fully read. [Sonnet check 2026-10-22: Age/quantity text in the earlier read was stripped by HTML parsing. Table 24 and the drug list both print 'PA - < 10 years and PA > 3 units/day' for quetiapine IR (Seroquel row, # brand), so adults 10 and older have no PA within 3 units/day. Legend (Table 24 footnotes): PD = preferred drug in the class, a trial is generally required before a non-PD agent, and PD agents can still carry PA; BP = brand preferred over generic; # = brand needs PA when an A-rated generic exists (generic payable); 'PA - < N years' = PA applies only below that age; 'PA - > N units/day' = PA applies only above that quantity; blank PA cell = no PA. Alternatives re-sorted: lurasidone and paliperidone ER carry age/quantity PA only, not plain PA. Verified.] [2026-10-22 review: sig replaced with label dosing by indication/titration.]

[Sonnet check 2026-10-22: Earlier pick (Uzedy) and every 'PD PA' reading were parse artifacts: the table prints 'PA - < 10 years and PA > N injections/...' for Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera, Erzofri, Uzedy, Perseris, Aristada, Risperdal Consta and Relprevv, so adults 10 and older have no PA within the limits. Only Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii and Rykindo carry plain PA. Repicked Invega Sustenna (PD, most commonly written LAI, no PA for adults within limit). Legend (Table 24 footnotes): PD = preferred drug in the class, a trial is generally required before a non-PD agent, and PD agents can still carry PA; BP = brand preferred over generic; # = brand needs PA when an A-rated generic exists (generic payable); 'PA - < N years' = PA applies only below that age; 'PA - > N units/day' = PA applies only above that quantity; blank PA cell = no PA. Haloperidol/fluphenazine decanoate have no row on the MHDL drug list; the MHDL introduction says a drug not on the List requires PA, and clinic-administered decanoates may bill under the medical benefit, so coverage is unconfirmed (not called not covered). Pick verified.] [2026-10-22 review: sig replaced with label dosing by indication/titration.]
